references.text: Parallel text about the Feast of Weeks (Shavuot) describing the same sacrifices: seven one-year-old lambs, one bull and two rams as a burnt offering to the Lord, together with a grain offering and a drink offering.
Similar sacrifice regulations for Passover with seven one-year-old unblemished lambs, one bull and two rams as a burnt offering.
Earlier in the same chapter, the requirements for the sacrificial lamb are described: it must be without blemish and one year old, together with a grain offering and a drink offering.
Instructions about daily burnt offerings of one-year-old lambs together with a grain offering and a drink offering as a pleasing aroma to the Lord.
Basic rules for burnt offerings from cattle that must be without blemish to be accepted by the Lord.
Requirement that sacrificial animals must be without blemish (תָּמִים) to be accepted as an offering to the Lord.
Regulations about grain offerings and drink offerings that should accompany burnt offerings from cattle as a pleasing aroma to the Lord.
The first time the expression 'pleasing aroma' (רֵיחַ נִיחֹחַ) is used in connection with Noah's burnt offering to the Lord.
Instructions about grain offerings (מִנְחָה) that were to accompany the burnt offering.
